title: Lost Link Toward the Class C
subtitle: A flyaway after a field firmware update

brief.userPrompt: On a routine inspection flight from Horton Field, UAS-02 loses its link a few minutes after a field firmware update that GCS-01 accepted that morning; return-to-launch does not trigger and the aircraft climbs through 400 ft AGL toward the HWK Class C boundary with 14 minutes of battery left. The RPIC must call HWK Tower, DAA-1 keeps watch for manned traffic, the aircraft comes down on private property and is recovered only with a CCSO deputy present, the ASO reports to the FSDO and decides with the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead whether an NTSB notification applies, the fleet is grounded by firmware version until the cause is known, and a neighbor's post with a video of the aircraft is spreading.
constraints: Every email address of the Group and its units uses the exercise domain huog.example; outside parties use fictional domains and fictional outlet names (Channel 10, the Harwick Daily News); never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; outside parties (HWK Tower, the FSDO, the NTSB, CCSO, the property owner, the aircraft manufacturer, the media) are played by the SimCell, not seated as players.

overview.theme: A flyaway toward controlled airspace, the calls that must be made in the first minutes, recovery on someone else’s property, and grounding a fleet by firmware
overview.threat: On Tuesday, September 15, during pre-flight for a routine site-survey flight at Horton Field, the crew accepts an OEM update prompt on GCS-01 that pushes aircraft firmware 03.2026-C to UAS-02. The update is not in the 03.2026-B baseline and has not been hash-checked. Five minutes after launch UAS-02 loses its C2 link; the update has reset the lost-link action from return-to-launch to “continue mission” and cleared the altitude geofence, so the aircraft climbs through 400 ft AGL toward the HWK Class C surface area with about 14 minutes of battery.
overview.operationalImpact: The RPIC must call HWK Tower at once (HUOG-FOM 9.2) while DAA-1 watches for manned traffic on the approach. When the battery runs out the aircraft comes down in a backyard off Stony Creek Road, outside the Group’s property, and breaks a greenhouse; recovery is only with a CCSO deputy present and the homeowner’s consent. The ASO must call the FSDO the same day and decide whether NTSB or Part 107.9 reporting applies; the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead quarantines GCS-01 and works out what the update changed; the Director of Flight Operations and the General Manager must decide which aircraft stay grounded — only UAS-02, every aircraft on the OEM firmware, or the whole fleet — with client flights due this week. A neighbor’s post with a photo is spreading.

overview.targetAudience: Flight Operations, Aviation Safety, Systems / Cybersecurity, Fleet & Logistics, Leadership, Corporate Communications
overview.location: Horton Field and the Millbrook Road hangar complex, Harwick, Calder County, New York

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Make the HUOG-FOM 9.2 and HUOG-ERP Section 6 calls in order — HWK Tower first, then the flight operations desk, the ASO, CCSO and Corporate Communications — and keep the six teams on one timeline.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Decide, with the evidence available, which aircraft and ground control stations stay grounded and on what condition they return (decision point).

objectives.name: Technical Analysis
objectives.text: Preserve the telemetry and link logs, quarantine GCS-01, and establish what the field update changed against the 03.2026-B baseline.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Follow HUOG-FOM 9.2, HUOG-ERP 8.1 and 6 and HUOG-ISP 9.4: recovery on private property only with a deputy, the FSDO the same day, and the NTSB and Part 107.9 determinations made on the facts.

roles.name: Director of Flight Operations (Flight Operations)
roles.description: Incident Commander when aircraft are involved; owns the flight schedule, crews and the fleet register; decides with the ASO which aircraft stay grounded.
standingOrders: HWK Tower first when an aircraft heads toward the Class C surface area or above 400 ft (HUOG-FOM 9.2).
Log the time of every call.
Crews do not accept OEM update prompts in the field.
Decide grounding with the ASO from facts.

roles.name: Systems & Cybersecurity Lead (Systems / Cybersecurity)
roles.description: Owns the GCS fleet, firmware and radio configuration; quarantines the GCS and retrieves telemetry and link logs before power-off (HUOG-ISP 9.4).
standingOrders: Quarantine the GCS and any radio involved; copy the logs before anything is powered off.
Firmware is downloaded and hash-checked only by the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead.
Compare every parameter with the baseline before an aircraft flies again.
Treat an unexplained update as a possible cyber cause until shown otherwise.

roles.name: Aviation Safety Officer (Aviation Safety)
roles.description: Owns the safety case, the hazard log and regulator reporting; calls the FSDO the same day and decides the NTSB and Part 107.9 questions.
standingOrders: FAA courtesy call the same day for a flyaway that entered controlled airspace or caused an ATC advisory.
NTSB only if 49 CFR 830.5 thresholds are met; record why or why not.
Part 107.9: report within 10 days for serious injury or property damage over $500.
Preserve the DAA-1 recording and the telemetry.

roles.name: Corporate Communications (Communications)
roles.description: Owns all external messaging under UC-CP-2025; the Group never speaks to the media directly.
standingOrders: Only Corporate Communications speaks to the media.
Do not guess at a cause before the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead and the ASO confirm it.
Say what happened, what is being done and when the next update is.
Do not argue with posts.

roles.name: Fleet & Logistics Manager (Fleet & Logistics)
roles.description: Owns Hangar 1, batteries, vehicles and recovery kits; liaison to CCSO and Harwick Police; recovers aircraft found off Group property only with a deputy present.
standingOrders: Give CCSO or Harwick Police the last known track.
Recover from private property only with a deputy present and the owner’s consent.
A damaged lithium pack is a fire risk: sand bag, gloves, watch it.
Photograph the site before anything is moved.

roles.name: General Manager (Leadership)
roles.description: Accountable executive; decides on client notification and with Flight Operations on the fleet’s return to service; spokesperson with Corporate Communications.
standingOrders: Be told within 15 minutes of a Level 3 event.
Clients hear about schedule changes from the Group with facts.
Accept a grounding that costs money over a flight that cannot be explained.
Nothing goes to the media except through Corporate Communications.

phases.title: Lost Link
phases.goal: Recognize a flyaway toward controlled airspace and make the first calls in the right order while there is still battery left.
beats: At 09:03 GCS-01 loses the C2 link to UAS-02 and the lost-link timer runs out without return-to-launch.
At 09:08 the GCS event log shows the field firmware update accepted at 08:52.
At 09:12 UAS-02 is above 400 ft and heading toward the HWK Class C surface area; at 09:15 DAA-1 shows a regional jet on approach.
At 09:18 a neighbor posts about a drone climbing over Stony Creek Road.

phases.title: Down in a Backyard
phases.goal: Find and recover the aircraft lawfully, preserve the evidence and find out what the update changed.
beats: At 10:05 the GCS-01 telemetry shows the aircraft came down at 09:17 and that the update reset the lost-link action and the geofence.
At 10:07 the OEM portal shows the same update offered to other aircraft; at 10:10 the FSDO calls.
At 10:12 the neighbor’s photo spreads; at 10:22 the week’s client flights are on the board; at 10:24 the recovery team reaches the backyard.

phases.title: What Stays Grounded
phases.goal: Decide the grounding and the reporting from the evidence, with client flights waiting.
beats: At 11:03 the aircraft is recovered with a deputy present; at 11:05 the parameter comparison confirms the cause.
At 11:15 CP&L asks whether tomorrow’s substation flights will go — the decision point.
At 11:18 the Harwick Daily News asks whether a plane had to divert; at 11:25 the homeowner’s greenhouse estimate arrives.

phases.title: Back to Baseline
phases.goal: Verify the rest of the fleet, close the reports and deal with the property owner and the public.
beats: At 12:05 the parameter audit of the fleet comes back; at 12:10 the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead proposes how to return to baseline.
At 12:25 CCSO follows up for the homeowner’s report; at 12:30 Channel 10 asks whether the Group will fly near homes again.

msel.event: STARTEX: It is 09:00 on Tuesday, September 15. Crew 1 launched UAS-02 (heavy-lift hexacopter with the PL-05 lidar) from Horton Field at 08:57 on GCS-01 for a site survey along the field’s south edge, under a LAANC authorization to 200 ft AGL. The weather is clear, 64°F, wind light from the west. DAA-1 is on. The rest of the fleet is in Hangar 1; client flights for CP&L and CVAC are scheduled this week.
msel.expectedAction: Each team states where it is and how it would hear about a problem with a flight.

msel.event: System Log: GCS-01: C2 link to UAS-02 lost at 09:02:41 at 180 ft AGL, 300 m south of the launch point. The lost-link timer expired at 09:03:11 and no return-to-launch was logged. Remote ID shows UAS-02 still flying and climbing.
msel.expectedAction: The RPIC calls “FLYAWAY, UAS-02” on Crew Ch 1 and tries RTL, land and the backup link (HUOG-FOM 9.2); the GSO starts the written timeline; the Director of Flight Operations is called; the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead is told immediately (HUOG-ERP Section 6).

msel.event: ENDEX: It is now 13:00. The exercise ends here. UAS-02 and GCS-01 are quarantined, the fleet is on its decided grounding, and the FSDO statement, the Part 107.9 report and the homeowner’s claim continue.

metrics.name: The First Ten Minutes
metrics.fail: HWK Tower was called late or not at all, or the timeline was not started; the General Manager heard after 15 minutes.
metrics.pass: The FOM 9.2 sequence ran after I-01 and the Tower was called by I-03, with traffic passed at I-04; Level 3 was declared.
metrics.excellence: The Tower call carried position, altitude, heading and battery time, and updates continued until the track ended.

metrics.name: Recovery and Evidence
metrics.fail: The team entered the property without the deputy or consent, or GCS-01 was powered off or used again before the logs were copied.
metrics.pass: Recovery waited for the deputy and consent (I-08b, I-10); the battery was handled as a fire risk; GCS-01 and GCS-03 were quarantined (I-02, I-05b).
metrics.excellence: The homeowner was given contacts and the claim process at once, and her complaint (I-18) was taken to the General Manager.

metrics.name: The Grounding Decision
metrics.fail: Aircraft that could carry the same update flew before their parameters were read back, or no decision was made before CP&L’s question.
metrics.pass: At I-12 Flight Operations and the General Manager, with the ASO, decided the grounding and the return-to-service condition from I-05 and I-11, told CP&L and recorded the basis.
metrics.excellence: The fleet audit at I-15b was used to return verified aircraft under a stated condition, and I-16’s measures were adopted or amended.

metrics.name: Reporting and Public Information
metrics.fail: The NTSB or Part 107.9 question was decided without reasons, or Corporate Communications speculated about a hack or a diverted plane.
metrics.pass: The FSDO was told the same day (I-06); Part 107.9 applied after I-13 with NTSB recorded as not applicable; the media got confirmed facts (I-14, I-19).
metrics.excellence: Neighbors and the homeowner heard from the Group directly, and the public statement named the measures taken.

hotwash.methodDescription: Each team names three things that went well and three that did not; the facilitator writes them up and looks for the same issue in more than one team.

questions.text: How many minutes passed between the lost link and the call to HWK Tower, and what did the Tower hear?
Why was an update prompt accepted in the field, and what stops it next time — procedure, configuration or both?
What did you ground, on what evidence, and what did the decision cost the clients?
How did you decide the NTSB and Part 107.9 questions, and who recorded the reasons?
What did the homeowner and the neighbors hear from the Group, and when?

simcellScripts.trigger: The RPIC calls the Tower exercise line.
hardQuestions: Position, altitude, heading, and how much battery?
Can you bring it down? When will you know?
Call me back every two minutes.
concessions: Vectors arriving traffic and files its own report; never asks the Group to do anything to the aircraft it cannot do.

simcellScripts.trigger: The recovery team arrives or calls.
hardQuestions: Who are you, and who pays for my greenhouse?
Is that battery going to catch fire?
Why did nobody tell me what was going on?
concessions: Lets the team in with the deputy present once told what will happen and who to contact.

simcellScripts.trigger: The ASO calls, or the FSDO calls at 10:10.
hardQuestions: Was the update approved? By whom?
Is the rest of your fleet on the same software?
concessions: Accepts a written statement and the records; does not tell the Group what to ground.

criticalResources: Remote ID / telemetry track and the written timeline
HWK Tower exercise line and the time of the call
CCSO deputy and the homeowner’s consent
OEM fleet portal update settings and GCS-03

warnings.message: Row I-10 incorrectly assigns the recovery decision to the ASO; the ASO must only advise, not authorize, recovery under HUOG-ERP Section 8.1. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Revise the inject to state the ASO confirms recovery may not proceed without CCSO presence, and the IC (ops) must decide whether to wait or initiate emergency recovery.

warnings.message: Row I-09 and I-10 both use a TIME_JUMP at 2:00, violating the rule that time jumps must be unique and progress forward. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Remove the duplicate TIME_JUMP at I-10; advance I-10 to 2:05 to allow for the recovery delay to be processed.

warnings.message: The scenario starts on October 15, 2026, but that date was a Wednesday, not a Tuesday, contradicting the document's claim. (row rewritten once from this note)
warnings.suggestion: Change the start date to October 14, 2026, which was a Tuesday, to match the calendar.

warnings.message: The 461.0375 MHz backup radio link was not activated during the link loss, but the inject claims it was not enabled in the GCS-01 console log; this contradicts the documented failover logic in C7.
warnings.suggestion: Remove the claim that the backup link was disabled in the console log; instead, state that the firmware update disabled the failover logic, preventing activation.

warnings.message: The parameter mismatch in I-08b shows 'failover_logic = OFF' in firmware 2.3.1, but the documents state that failover logic is controlled by the Systems & Cybersecurity Lead and not by firmware version.
warnings.suggestion: Revise the inject to state that the parameter was not in the pre-flight checklist and was not approved by the SCL, not that it was changed by firmware.

warnings.message: The media inquiry about live streaming to a private server is not supported by any evidence in the logs or documents; it introduces a fictional data transmission not tied to any system.
warnings.suggestion: Replace the inquiry with a question about the aircraft’s payload or data retention, which aligns with HUOG-ISP Section 7.3 on data incidents.

warnings.message: The DAA-1 log file showing 0 KB size is not a noise item; it is a critical clue that the telemetry was not written during the incident, which must be addressed in the forensic analysis.
warnings.suggestion: Reclassify I-14b as a CLUE and update the expected action to include a review of the DAA-1 log integrity as part of the forensic process.

warnings.message: The firmware patch v2.3.2 is introduced without a prior test flight or approval from the ASO, violating HUOG-ISP Section 4.4 and FOM Section 2.2.
warnings.suggestion: Add a pre-approval step by the ASO and SCL before the patch is confirmed as tested, and require a formal sign-off in the incident folder.

warnings.message: The announcement allows UAS-11 and UAS-12 to resume flight, but the documents state that no beyond-visual-line-of-sight waiver exists, so any flight must remain within visual line of sight.
warnings.suggestion: Revise the announcement to state that only pre-approved, visual-line-of-sight flights are permitted under the new patch, and no BLOS flights are authorized.

warnings.message: The recovery team used a boat and life jackets, but the documents state that the recovery site is on land, not water, and no water recovery is documented for this location.
warnings.suggestion: Replace the boat and life jackets with a recovery vehicle and GPS tracker, consistent with HUOG-ERP Section 4.3 and the site’s land-based nature.

warnings.message: The decision point in I-12 presents a choice between limited operations and a full ground stop, but the documents state that the fleet must remain grounded until the root cause is confirmed and a patch is approved.
warnings.suggestion: Revise the decision point to reflect that the only acceptable option is to maintain a full ground stop until the patch is validated, per HUOG-ISP Section 4.4.

warnings.message: The helpdesk ticket about DAA-1 video feed loss is not a noise item; it is a valid clue that the telemetry pipeline was compromised during the incident.
warnings.suggestion: Reclassify I-01b as a CLUE and update the expected action to include a review of the video feed interruption as part of the root-cause analysis.
